messages:
emma_support: heads-up — Streamleap is seeing persistent 429s in prod since 03:10 UTC after their new worker rollout. customer says errors spike exactly at minute boundaries and during load tests.

alex_m: can you paste a request/response sample and the x-rate-limit headers if available?

emma_support: yep — grabbed one from the customer logs: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.test
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx
Request-Id: rl-req-9fb2

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-rpm: 120/120
x-rate-limit-tpm: 10000/10000
retry-after: 3
content-type: application/json
{
  \"error\": \"Quota exceeded: client RPM\"
}
```

priya_ops: hmm rpm==limit and tpm fine — looks like a short per-minute burst. Are they reusing a single API key across many parallel clients?

emma_support: customer confirms they spawned 40 ephemeral workers after a deploy, each fanouts 15 requests per second for a few seconds (no jitter).

danielle: that explains it — token-level RPM is getting hammered. Recommend temporary mitigations: 1) client-side jitter + exponential backoff, 2) reduce concurrency on workers, 3) server-side aggregation to batch requests.

alex_m: long term options: increase their RPM quota on their plan or move them to a dedicated pool. Short-term we can apply a soft throttle on the key (burst smoothing) for ~1 hour if they approve.

emma_support: they asked for a quick repro to help devs fix it — any easy way to reproduce on our side?

priya_ops: reproduce: run a small script that opens N persistent connections and fires M requests at the top of each minute — e.g.,
```bash
for i in {1..40}; do (while true; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"x\"}'; sleep 0.2; done) & done
```
This will show 429s when RPM limit is hit. Add a random sleep 0-200ms to mitigate.

emma_support: customer also wants guidance for retry headers — we should point them to using Retry-After + 429 backoff policy. I'll send a short checklist.

danielle: checklist: 1) inspect x-rate-limit-* headers, 2) implement client jittered backoff (expo capped), 3) shard API keys per worker pool if possible, 4) use batching/aggregation, 5) request quota bump or dedicated capacity if steady high RPM.

quota-bot: Automated note: customer token rl-req-9fb2 has 3 recent 429s in last 60s — flagged for ops review.

alex_m: I'll draft an email with repro steps + suggested code snippet and ask for permission to temporarily smooth their key. :+1:

emma_support: thanks — looping in customer now, will update thread with their decision. :eyes:
